sources.entry: iTerm 2 - Terminal emulator for macOS that does amazing things.

summary.one_liner: iTerm2 is a feature-rich terminal emulator and replacement for the default Terminal app on macOS.
summary.what_it_does: iTerm2 is a macOS terminal emulator that adds tmux integration, where tmux -CC windows and tabs appear as native macOS windows and sessions persist across crashes and disconnects. Shell integration tracks commands, directories, hostnames and usernames, enabling click-to-download via SCP, drag-and-drop uploads, per-host command history and marks at each prompt. It includes an built-in LLM AI chat window that can optionally read terminal contents, inline image display (including animated GIFs via imgcat), and a built-in web browser profile type. Other features include automatic profile switching based on host or directory, a system-wide hotkey window that slides down from a screen edge, per-session status bars, regex triggers, smart selection, Vim-like copy mode, Instant Replay of terminal history, and a Python scripting API. Sessions run in long-lived server processes so shells survive iTerm2 crashes or upgrades.
use_cases: replace the default macOS Terminal app
persist terminal sessions across crashes or SSH disconnects
use tmux with native macOS windows and tabs
upload and download files over SSH from the terminal
automate terminal behavior with Python scripts
view images inline in the terminal
switch terminal colors per server or environment
how_to_run: Download the latest release from iterm2.com/downloads
git clone the repository (for building from source)
notable: Native tmux -CC integration that turns tmux windows into real macOS windows
Sessions run in long-lived server processes so shells survive app crashes and upgrades
Automatic profile switching based on hostname, user, directory or running command
Instant Replay to scrub back through terminal history with timestamps
Python scripting API for custom status bar components, triggers and menus
caveats: Source builds need Xcode and several toolchains; make setup installs Homebrew, Rust and others and may require sudo
Development builds may be less stable than official releases
Re-running make paranoid-deps is needed whenever the active Xcode version changes
